questions.q: A body weight <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>, is projected vertically upwards from earth's surface to reach a height above the earth which is equal to nine times the radius of earth. The weight of the body at that height will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Final distance from the centre of earth wil be R+9R=10R.

Now acceleration due to gravity at any height(distance from centre r) is given by,

g=GMr2.

Therefore,

g'=GM10R2

Now, value of g at surface will be, GMR2.

Hence,

g'=g100.

Then, W'=mg'=mg100=W100

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : The escape velocities of planet A and B are same. But A and B are of unequal mass.

Reason R: The product of their mass and radius must be same. M1R1=M2R2 In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>

Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is NOT the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Ve=2GMR

M1R1=M2R2

M1R2=M2R1

Hence reason R is not correct.

questions.q: The time period of a satellite, revolving above earth's surface at a height equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> will be (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo></math> radius of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The velocity of the satellite revolving round the Earth at a height r from the centre of the Earth is given by

v=GMr   ...1

The formula to calculate the time period in the circular orbit is given by

T=2πrv   ...2

In this case: r=R+R=2R

Substitute the expression for the velocity from equation (1) into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required time period.

T=2πrGMr=2π×2RgR2=4πR2πR=42R=32R

questions.q: Consider a binary star system of star <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and star <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> with masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></msub></math> revolving in a circular orbit of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></msub></math> are the time period of star <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and star <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> respectively, then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
1) From the centre of mass, we get

M1R1=M2R2------1

2) Force acting on both starts i.e. gravitational force and centripetal force are balanced.

GM1M2R2=M1V12R1=M1V12R1------2

As we know, V1=2πR1T1&V2=2πR2T2

Substituting equation 3 in equation 2, we get 

M1R1T12=M1R2T22------4

From equation 1, we conclude in eqution 4

T12=T22  or  T1=T2

questions.q:
The approximate height from the surface of earth at which the weight of the body becomes 13 of its weight on the surface of earth is :
[Radius of earth R=6400 km and 3=1.732]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The variation of the acceleration due to gravity with height h is given by,

g'=g1+hR2.

Since the weight at given height is 13 of the weight at the surface

⇒g'=g3⇒g1+hR2=g3⇒1+hR=3⇒h=R3-1=6400×1.732-1=4685 km

questions.q:
Assume that the earth is a solid sphere of uniform density and a tunnel is dug along its diameter throughout the earth. It is found that when a particle is released in this tunnel, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The mass of the particle is 100 g. The time period of the motion of the particle will be (approximately)

(take g=10 ms-2, radius of earth =6400 km)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The gravitational force acting on a particle of mass m at a distance r (<R) from the centre of Earth is

F=-GM'mr2  ....(1)

where M' is the mass of portion of Earth enclosed by a sphere of radius r concentric with Earth. Here - sign indicates radially inward direction of force.

Taking the density of Earth to be uniform

M'4πr3=M4πR3

⇒M'=Mr3R3   ....(2)

Substituting M' from equation 2 into equation 1:

F=-GMmR3 r

Which is similar to the equation of motion F=-kx with k=GMmR3=mgR (∵g=GMR2)

For such motion, the time period is given by:

T=2πmk

Substituting k from above,

T=2πRg

Putting the values, we get

T=2×3.146400×10310=2×3.14×800≈1 hour 24 minutes

questions.q: The mass of the moon is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>144</mn></mfrac></math> times the mass of a planet and its diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>16</mn></mfrac></math> times the diameter of a planet. If the escape velocity on the planet is v, the escape velocity on the moon will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, escape velocity is given by, vescape=2GMR

Now, vplanet=2GMR=v

vMoon=2GM×16144×R=132GMR=v3

questions.q: An object is taken to a height above the surface of earth at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mi>R</mi></math> from the centre of the earth. Where radius of earth, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math>. The percentage decrease in the weight of the object will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at height h is given by, g'=g1+hR2

For distance from the centre r=54R height h=R4,

⇒g'=g1+142=1625g

Change in weight 

∆W=mg-mg'⇒∆W=mg1-1625

⇒∆W=925mg

Percentage change =925×100%

=36%

questions.q: A mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is placed at the center of a uniform spherical shell of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. If the gravitational potential at a point, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the center is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Use the formula of the gravitational potential in terms of universal gravitational constant, V=-GMR⇒Vp=-G(100)50-G(50)25=-4G.

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the radius of the earth and the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then the length of the second's pendulum at a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi></math> from the surface of earth will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at the given height, g'=GM3R2=19GMR2=19g, where g is acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the Earth.

Now, time period is given by, T=2πlg'

Also the time period of second pendulum is 2 sec.

Therefore, T=2 sec

Then, 2=2πlg×9

⇒l=19 m

questions.q: A planet having mass 9 Me and radius 4Re, where Me and Re are mass and radius of earth respectively, has escape velocity in km s-1 given by: (Given escape velocity on earth Ve=11.2×103 m s-1)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The escape velocity on earth is given by Ve =2GMeRe

Escape velocity for the planet is

V'esc=2G(9Me)4Re   ...(i)

The escape velocity of earth is Ve=11.2×103 m s-1

From equation (i)

V'esc=942GMeRe=32×11.2×103 m s-1⇒V'esc=16.8 km s-1

questions.q: An astronaut takes a ball of mass $m$ from earth to space. He throws the ball into a circular orbit about earth at an altitude of $318.5 \mathrm{~km}$. From earth's surface to the orbit, the change in total mechanical energy of the ball is $x \frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}$. The value of $x$ is (take $\left.\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}=6370 \mathrm{~km}\right)$ :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{h}=318.5 \approx\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{20}\right) \\ & \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}} \\ & \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{2\left(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{h}\right)}=\frac{-\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{2\left(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}+\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{20}\right)} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-10 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}\end{aligned}$
Change in total mechanical energy
$\begin{aligned} & =\mathrm{TE}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{TE}_{\mathrm{i}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{\operatorname{Re}}\left[1-\frac{10}{21}\right]=\frac{11 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{21 \operatorname{Re}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two planets A and B of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>R</mi></math> have densities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>ρ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> respectively. The ratio of acceleration due to gravity at the surface of B to A is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity is 

g=GMR2=4πGRρ3⇒g∝ρ·R

Thus, the ratio is 

⇒gBgA=1.5Rρ2ρR=12×1.5=0.75⇒gBgA=34

questions.q: If earth has a mass nine times and radius twice to the of a planet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> will be the minimum velocity required by a rocket to pull out of gravitational force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>, where ve is escape velocity on earth. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the escape velocityve for the Earth is given by

ve= 2GMeRe.......................(1)

where, G is the Universal Gravitational constant, Me is the mass and Re is the radius of Earth.

The formula for the escape velocity vesc of any planet is given by

vesc= 2GMR........................(2)

where, M is the mass and R is the radius of the planet.

Given that the mass of the planet is 9 times the mass of the Earth and the radius of the planet is 2 times the radius of the Earth.

Substitute Me9 for M and Re2 for R into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the escape velocity for the planet in terms of that in Earth.

vesc= 2GMe9Re2= 292GMeRe= 23ve.....................(3)

Comparing equation (3) with the given expression, it can be written that

x= 2.

If the weight of an object on earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>, the weight of the same object on that planet will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Density is same

M=43πR3ρ, 2m=43πR'3ρ

R'=213R

W=GMmR2

W2=G2MmR'2

W2=213W

questions.q: A body of mass is taken from earth surface to the height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> equal to twice the radius of earth <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></math>, the increase in potential energy will be : (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo></math> acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential energy of a particle at a distance r (>Re)  from the centre of Earth is,

U=-GMemr

Initially, the particle is at a height Re from the surface. Therefore, r=Re.

∴Ui=-GMemRe

When height is increased to 2Re from surface, r=2Re+Re=3Re

∴Uf=-GMem3Re

Thus, the change in potential energy is

∆U=Uf-Ui=-GMem3Re+GMemRe=23GMemRe=23GMeRe2mRe=23mgRe as g=GMeRe2

questions.q: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place $\mathrm{R}$ height above earth surface has time period of $T_1=4 \mathrm{~s}$. $T_2$ would be it's time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height $2 \mathrm{R}$ from earth surface. Choose the correct relation $[R=$ radius of earth $]$ :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{GM}}(2 \mathrm{R})^2} \\ & \mathrm{~T}_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{GM}}(3 \mathrm{R})^2} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The ratio of escape velocity of a planet to the escape velocity of earth will be:-

Given: Mass of the planet is 16 times mass of earth and radius of the planet is 4 times the radius of earth.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the escape velocity is given by

ve=2GMR   ...1

For the Earth, it is given by

veE=2GMERE...2

 and, for the planet, it is given by

veP=2GMPRP...3

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

veEveP=MEMP×RPRE   ...4

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (4) to obtain the required ratio.

veEveP=ME16ME×4RERE=12⇒veP:veE= 2:1

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> above the earth if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>R</mi></math> (Radius of earth) is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity g' at a height h from the surface of Earth is given by

g'=GM(R+h)2   ...1

Use the method of binomial expansion to obtain the approximate expression for the acceleration due to gravity at a particular height from the surface of the Earth.

g'=GMR21+hR2= GMR21+hR-2≈GMR21-2hR   ...2

The formula to calculate the acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the Earth is given by

g=GMR2   ...(3)

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and simplify to obtain the required relation.

g'g=GMR21-2hRGMR2= 1-2hR⇒g'=g1-2hR

questions.q: Two satellites <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> move round the earth in the same orbit. The mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is twice the mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math>. The quantity which is same for the two satellites will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the speed of a satellite while revolving around the Earth is given by

v=GMeR   ...1

where, v is the speed, G is the Gravitational constant, Me is the mass of the Earth, R is the radius of the orbit.

As can be seen from the equation, speed is independent of mass of satellite.

Hence, the speed of the satellites will be the same.

questions.q: The weight of a body on the surface of the earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The gravitational force on it when taken at a height, from the surface of earth, equal to one-fourth the radius of the earth is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity changes as one goes to a height from the surface of the earth. Let the new acceleration due to gravity be g'. The formula for acceleration due to gravity at a height is given by g'=gR2R+h2

The weight of the body on surface is W=mg=100 N

The weight at the given height is W=mg'.

⇒W'=100×R2R+R42⇒W'=100×R225R216=64 N

questions.q: The escape velocities of two planets <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></math> are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn></math>. If the ratio of their radii respectively is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn></math>, then the ratio of acceleration due to gravity of planet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> to the acceleration of gravity of planet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the mass M of any planet of radius R and density ρ, considering it to be a sphere, is given by

M= 43πR3ρ.....................(1)

The escape velocity vA for planet A can be expressed as

VA=2GMARA=2GρA43πRA3RA=CρA.RA............................(2)

where, G is Gravitational constant and C= 8πG3 is a constant.

Similarly, the escape velocity vB of planet B can be expressed as

vB= CρBRB......................(3)

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and solve with the known parameters to obtain the ratio of the densities of the planets.

VAVB=CρARACρBRBρAρB= VARBVBRAρAρB= VARBVBRA2= 12×312= 94............................(4)

The acceleration due to gravity gA for planet A is given by

gA=GMARA2=G43πRA3×ρARA2= C22ρARA..........................(5)

Similarly, the acceleration due to gravity gB can be expressed as

gB= C22ρBRB...........................(6)

Divide equation (5) by equation (6) and solve with the help of known parameters to calculate the required ratio of the accelerations due to gravity in both the planets.

gAgB=C22ρARAC22ρBRB=ρAρBRARB= 94×13=34

=14×R2R1=34

questions.q: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> is the time period of simple pendulum on the earth's surface. Its time period becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></math> when taken to a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of a simple pendulum at Earth's surface is given by

T=2πlg.

When distance from centre of Earth, i.e., at h=R, acceleration due to gravity is g'=g1+hR2=g22=g4

Now, time period is  xT=2πlg4

⇒xT=2×2πlg

⇒xT=2T⇒x=2

Thus, x=2.
